messages.subject: Hello, world!
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I shall do the honours and publish this first message.

I also take this opportunity to announce that the time-specific resource availability issue (#21) is closed. The new feature is stable and fully functional. The proper tests have been added and the changes have been merged into the master branch.

Along the path, there have been some fixes and improvements (check the NEWS <https://github.com/Enchufa2/simmer/blob/master/NEWS.md>), so I'm planning to unroll a version 3.2.1 this weekend into CRAN. Thoughts?

Finally, I would like to tackle the issue #45 (batching) as a next step, because several useRs have already asked about it.

Regards,
Iñaki

messages.subject: Time now() in a trajectory.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shawn,

Of course it is, whenever you define the environment *before* running the simulation. For instance, this won't work:

t <- create_trajectory() %>%
  timeout(function() print(env %>% now()))

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_generator("dummy", t, function() 1) %>%
  run(4)
Because the global "env" is not available at runtime: the simulation runs *and then* the resulting object is assigned to "env". You need to assign first, then run. So this will work:
t <- create_trajectory() %>%
  timeout(function() print(env %>% now()))

env <- simmer() %>%
  add_generator("dummy", t, function() 1)

env %>% run(4)
And you'll get "1, 2, 3", as expected. However, as a general rule of good practice, I recommend you to instantiate the environment always in the first place, because the code becomes more readable:
# First, instantiate the environment
env <- simmer()

# Here I'm using it
t <- create_trajectory() %>%
  timeout(function() print(env %>% now()))

# And finally, run it
env %>%
  add_generator("dummy", t, function() 1) %>%
  run(3)

Regards,
Iñaki

2016-04-27 16:20 GMT+02:00 Garbett, Shawn P  <>:
Iñaki Úcar,

Is it possible to check the current time of a simulation inside a trajectory? The now() function depends on an environment, not the current trajectory.

Shawn Garbett | Sr. App Developer | Biostatistics | Vanderbilt University

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Time now() in a trajectory.
messages.body_plain:
And for the sake of completeness, here it is another set of examples, very related to this issue, in response to Lindsay Mico:

> First, I'd like to use functions in the simulation based on the current sim time.  The most obvious use would to be create a generator function that is dependent on what the current time is in the simulation.  In my experiments with now(), I have been successful using it after the simulation has been run, but not embedding it into either the trajectory or the generator.
env <- simmer("SuperDuperSim") # you may do this at the beginning as a general rule of good practice

t0 <- create_trajectory("my trajectory") %>%
  timeout(0)

my_generator <- function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() {
  if (now(env) %% 5 == 0)
    print <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/print>(sprintf <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/sprintf>("now() is a multiple of 5: %f", now(env)))
  1 # one time unit between arrivals
}

env %>%
  add_generator("instant-traveler", t0, my_generator) %>%
  run(until=10)
> A related question is how to run user defined functions inside a simulation.  For example, it would be useful to export a plot every time an entity reaches a given point in a trajectory.

This one is funny. :)
library <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/library>(animation <http://inside-r.org/packages/cran/animation>)

env <- simmer("SuperDuperSim")

plot_and_wait <- function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() {
  if (now(env) > 1)
    print <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/print>(plot_resource_usage(env, "checkin", steps=T))
  rnorm <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/rnorm>(1, mean <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/mean> = 7, sd <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/sd> = 2)
}

t0 <- create_trajectory("my trajectory") %>%
  seize("checkin", 1) %>%
  timeout(plot_and_wait) %>%
  release("checkin", 1)

env %>%
  add_generator("traveler", t0, function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() rexp <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/rexp>(1,rate=.625)) %>%
  add_resource("checkin", 5)

# use your own path here for the GIF
saveGIF(run(env, until=50), interval <http://inside-r.org/packages/cran/interval> = .2, movie.name <http://movie.name>="trace.gif")

> Or even to change the structure of the trajectory itself based on queue size or wait time.

You cannot change the trajectory object, but you can define many options in one with a branch:
env <- simmer("SuperDuperSim")

decide <- function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() {
  if (env %>% get_queue_count("checkin") <= 3)
    1         # first trajectory of the branch
  else 2   # second trajectory of the branch
}

t0 <- create_trajectory("my trajectory") %>%
  branch(decide, merge <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/merge>=c <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/c>(T, T),
         create_trajectory("seize") %>%
           seize("checkin", 1) %>%
           timeout(1) %>%
           release("checkin", 1),
         create_trajectory("skip") %>%
           timeout(function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() { print <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/print>("So much travellers waiting... I desist"); 0 })
         )

env %>%
  add_generator("traveler", t0, function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() rexp <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/rexp>(1,rate=.625)) %>%
  add_resource("checkin", 1) %>%
  run()

> Last question - as an experiment I tried writing a for loop that calls onestep n times, increments a counter variable 'test'.  In the code below I had hoped to assign this variable as an attribute at each step.  However as far as I can tell, the actual value of the variable is assigned at the time the environment is instantiated, rather than simply the variable itself.  If this doesn't make sense let me know.

As in all previous examples, you need to define a function for the set_attribute activity, not a static value:

env <- simmer("SuperDuperSim")

t0 <- create_trajectory("my trajectory") %>%
  timeout(function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() runif <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/runif>(1, min <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/min>=2, max <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/max>=3)) %>%
  seize("checkin", 1) %>%
  set_attribute("test", function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() test) %>%
  timeout(function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() rnorm <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/rnorm>(1, mean <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/mean> = 7, sd <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/sd> = 2)) %>%
  release("checkin", 1)

env %>%
  add_resource("checkin", 5) %>%
  add_generator("traveler", t0, function <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/function>() rexp <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/stats/rexp>(1,rate=.625),mon = 2)

test <- 0
for(i in 1:100){

  env<-onestep(env)
  test <- test+1
  print <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/base/print>(test)
}

get_mon_attributes(env)

Regards,
Iñaki
